hook: A gift for the gardener who has everything
hook_sub: Knees and backs wear out before the garden does

slides.t: A garden kneeler is a padded bench. Flip it one way and you kneel on soft foam instead of cold, wet ground.
Flip it over and it becomes a low seat. Good for weeding, planting and long jobs close to the soil.
The side frames work as handles. Push on them to get down and back up without straining knees or back.
A sturdy steel frame, thick foam that wipes clean, a weight rating that fits, and a frame that folds flat.
It folds flat, so it fits under the tree. A practical gift they will reach for every spring.

hook_sub: Easy to avoid if you plan in winter

slides.t: Keep beds about 4 feet wide. You should reach the middle from either side without stepping on the soil.
Most vegetables want 6 to 8 hours of direct sun. Watch where the sun falls before you set a bed down.
Fill with a mix of good topsoil and compost, not just bagged potting mix. Top it up with compost each year.
Raised beds drain fast. Check the soil often in summer, and mulch to hold moisture in.
Rust-resistant metal or untreated rot-resistant wood, at least 12 inches deep for root crops.
